transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-08-20
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Park (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood CSM), Jonas Li (Redwood Eng); Liam O'Connor (Atlas Infra), Sofia Martinez (Atlas Sec), Ravi Patel (Atlas ML), Evelyn Wong (Atlas PM)

Auto-summary: Weekly POC check-in to review pilot status for Redwood Private (VPC) deployment; topics: networking, routing/canary, agent upgrade, KV cache perf, security questions.

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call -- we got Atlas and Redwood here, awesome. Agenda: network diagram updates, routing issue that popped up last week, planned agent upgrade in staging, and KV cache numbers Ravi promised.
[00:18] Liam (Atlas): Hey, yep on our side. Quick note -- we found some outbound egress across AZs that cost us more, so that's top of mind.
[00:30] Maya (Redwood): Right, that's likely the routing policy fallback. We saw a similar behavior where requests hit the fallback mesh because we had a partial CIDR overlap in the peering table.
[00:45] Sofia (Atlas): We can share the peering CIDRs but need to ensure least-privilege rules. Also the security team wants to confirm KMS key flow for model logs -- is Redwood using customer-managed keys?
[01:05] Alex (Redwood): For Private we support both CMK via KMS and Redwood-managed keys. We'll send a KMS flow diagram. Note: when using CMK you need the correct grant for the agent role.
[01:22] Ravi (Atlas): Quick question - on the KV cache warming, how sticky is the cache across restarts? We saw TTLs drop after a patch.
[01:35] Jonas (Redwood): Good point. The runtime persists hot entries in the KV across soft restarts if the eviction policy is warm, but a full node replacement will flush unless the prefix cache is backed by our optional redis layer. For your pilot we're on native KV only, so we expect some cold starts after full host replacement.
[01:58] Evelyn (Atlas): That aligns w/ what we measured. We saw p95 token latency jump on redeploys. I put some numbers in the shared sheet.
[02:12] Maya (Redwood): OK we'll look at the sheet after. On routing, we want to propose a canary policy that pins traffic by shard to avoid cross-AZ fallback. Basically early traffic stays local with a 5% global spillover.
[02:30] Liam (Atlas): Sounds reasonable. We just need the exact routing policy template.
[02:40] Alex (Redwood): I'll send the template + example for your infra. Also note that the issue last week was an overlapping /20 in peering config that made the route prefer the other VPC in one AZ.
[02:55] Sofia (Atlas): Sorry, can you repeat the /20 bit - sometimes our CIDR notes are messy.
[03:05] Maya (Redwood): Yeah, short version: one of the Atlas subnets sits in a CIDR range that the peer was also advertising, so the route lookup picked the wrong next hop when the primary host hit transient CPU pressure.
[03:20] Ravi (Atlas): Oof, that explains it. We'll audit subnets and push a cleaned list.
[03:30] Alex (Redwood): Great, Liam, can you take owning the subnet list action?
[03:34] Liam (Atlas): Yep, I'll share by Friday.
[03:40] [04:00] Jonas (Redwood): About the agent upgrade - we plan to move from agent 2.1.0 to 2.2.0 next week in staging. 2.2.0 contains a routing fix and improved KV persistency. We want to run a rollback test too.
[04:16] Evelyn (Atlas): Any breaking changes? We have a policy that major upgrades need a 48-hour maintenance window.
[04:25] Maya (Redwood): No breaking schema changes; it is a minor release but we will still run a canary and a canary rollback plan. We recommend a 2-hour window for staging and 4 hours for prod.
[04:40] Sofia (Atlas): Security asked about the audit logs retention and whether audit events are sent to our SIEM - can we forward to a customer S3 or syslog?
[04:52] Alex (Redwood): Yes, we can push audit events to your S3 or to the syslog collector. For Private deployments we support both, and we encrypt at rest with your CMK if provided. We'll send the integration guide.
[05:10] [06:00] Ravi (Atlas): On performance - I ran the KV-cache microbench. Numbers: cold p95 tokens ~ 420ms, warm ~ 88ms, but during redeploy we saw p95 up to 1.1s. Sheet link in chat.
[06:25] Maya (Redwood): Thanks, those are helpful. The warm numbers are within expectation; the redeploy spike suggests we should enable prefix caching or add the redis-backed store if you need faster warmups.
[06:40] Liam (Atlas): Does redis-backed require additional infra we can't host? We prefer to keep infra minimal.
[06:50] Jonas (Redwood): It is optional. The redis-backed store can be hosted in your VPC as a small managed instance. It reduces cold-starts significantly but adds another component to maintain. Tradeoff to discuss.
[07:05] Alex (Redwood): We can also tune eviction policy to keep more hot prefixes for your access pattern; Maya will propose config lines.
[07:15] [08:00] Priya (Redwood): Quick CSM note - success metrics for the pilot: stable p95 <= 120ms for warm requests, <2 incidents/week, and no security non-conformances. Are those acceptable?
[08:30] Evelyn (Atlas): Warm p95 120ms is tough for some of our high-throughput endpoints, but as a pilot target it's OK. We'll flag which routes are high-priority.
[08:45] Sofia (Atlas): Also for compliance, we need SOC2-like evidence: audit log retention, SSO flows, RBAC mappings. Please include an artifact pack.
[09:00] Alex (Redwood): We'll share our security pack and the KMS flow diagram.
[09:10] [10:00] Maya (Redwood): Routing deep-dive plan: 1) send policy template, 2) run staging canary with pinned shard, 3) monitor cross-AZ egress for 48h, 4) rollback if egress > threshold. I'll prepare step-by-step.
[10:25] Liam (Atlas): For monitoring what thresholds do you recommend? Egress > 3% or p95 latency delta > 20%?
[10:40] Maya (Redwood): Start with egress > 2% or p95 increase > 15% as fail criteria for the canary. We'll calibrate after first run.
[10:55] Ravi (Atlas): Also we need to test model fallback - if the primary model variant is out, what's the automatic fallback behavior?
[11:10] Jonas (Redwood): We have automatic fallback to a smaller quantized variant by policy. You can set per-route fallback tiers; we'll show defaults in the runbook.
[11:25] Evelyn (Atlas): Great. Can we get a short doc on quantization differences and quality expectations? Some PMs are worried about regression.
[11:40] Alex (Redwood): Yes, we'll include model-quality notes and the eval harness link.
[11:50] [12:00] Sofia (Atlas): One more security ask: will Redwood rotate TLS certs, or do we manage them?
[12:10] Alex (Redwood): For Private, customers manage the certs if they prefer, or Redwood can manage and rotate certs under an SLA. We'll add the options to the doc pack.
[12:25] [13:00] Priya (Redwood): Recap and next steps: Alex send network diagram + security pack; Maya prepare routing canary plan; Jonas schedule staging upgrade; Atlas to provide bastion IPs and CIDR cleanup; Ravi to upload KV perf; Priya to share dashboard link.
[13:40] Liam (Atlas): Confirmed on our side. Thanks.
[13:50] Alex (Redwood): Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links and proposed times.
[14:00] Meeting end.

Shared artifacts mentioned:
- Pilot perf sheet: https://drive.company/atlas-redwood/pilot-perf (uploaded by Ravi)
- Redwood VPC runbook & routing templates: https://redwood.app/internal/vpc-runbook (will be shared)
